title: How to Actually Stick to Your Gym Membership in NZ — Practical Tips
meta_desc: Stick to your gym membership in NZ with practical tips, habit formation and accountability strategies
intro: With gym memberships in NZ ranging from $15 to $50 per week, making the most of your membership requires more than just a financial commitment. Many Kiwis struggle to stick to their gym routine, with some gyms like Les Mills and Jetts having contract terms of up to 12 months. However, with the right mindset and strategies, you can achieve your fitness goals and make the most of your membership.

sections.heading: Habit Formation Strategies
sections.body: Forming a habit takes time and consistency, but it can be achieved by setting realistic goals and tracking progress. Start by committing to a specific workout schedule, such as 3 times a week, and gradually increase the frequency and intensity over time. You can also find a workout buddy or join a fitness class to stay motivated and accountable.

sections.heading: Accountability Strategies
list: Find a workout buddy or personal trainer
Join a fitness class or group training session
Track progress through mobile apps or fitness trackers
Set realistic goals and reward yourself for achieving them

sections.heading: Making the Most of Your NZ Gym Membership
sections.body: Different gyms in NZ offer varying levels of service and amenities, so it's essential to choose a gym that meets your needs and budget. For example, Anytime Fitness has over 50 locations across NZ and offers 24/7 access, with memberships starting from $20 per week. On the other hand, CityFitness has a more comprehensive range of amenities, including pools and group fitness classes, with memberships starting from $30 per week.

Finding the Right Gym for You
sections.body: With so many gyms to choose from in NZ, it can be overwhelming to decide which one is right for you. Consider factors such as location, amenities, and price when making your decision. You can also read reviews and ask for referrals from friends or family members who have experience with different gyms. For example, you can check out our guide to Les Mills NZ to learn more about their services and prices.
